questions.question: What is the legal and economic origin of every CNY in the account?
questions.known: PRC law taxes enumerated categories including wages, services, business, interest, dividends, rent, property transfer and other income at different rules.
questions.missing: Your contracts, statements, sale records, gift/inheritance documents and source-of-funds chronology.
questions.why: The origin decides whether the documented-income, emigrant/inheritance, or another approval route fits, and whether PRC tax was due.
questions.discover: Download all account statements; assemble employment contracts, payslips, invoices, sale agreements, gift or inheritance papers; ask the bank which source documents it will accept in writing.

questions.question: Was all PRC tax on the underlying income or asset paid, and is there an official tax certificate?
questions.known: SAFE's documented-income rule requires source materials including tax documents; property-transfer guides require a tax certificate or tax-payment proof; the tax authority issues a completion certificate and late tax carries a daily surcharge.
questions.missing: Your 完税证明 / tax certificate and whether any amount is overdue.
questions.why: Without tax proof a bank may refuse FX purchase; unpaid tax can grow through surcharge and enforcement.
questions.discover: Request official tax records and a 完税证明 from the competent tax bureau; reconcile them to the source documents; ask a PRC tax professional to certify whether anything remains due.

questions.question: Are you a PRC tax resident, a foreign individual in China, or a foreign permanent-residence ID holder?
questions.known: The statute defines a domestic individual to include qualifying foreigners resident for at least 183 days; PRC tax residence uses a 183-day rule; only foreign permanent-residence ID holders are stated to use the annual purchase convenience quota in the SAFE FAQ.
questions.missing: Passport, visas, residence records, days present, and permanent-residence card status.
questions.why: This determines whether the US$50,000 annual quota, documented-income route, or another route is even available.
questions.discover: Build a day-count calendar from entry/exit stamps; keep passport, residence permit and permanent-residence card copies; ask the bank to state your classification in writing.

questions.question: Did you acquire foreign citizenship/permanent residence and cancel a PRC hukou before the funds arose?
questions.known: Emigrant property transfer is for lawful property owned before the immigration status; the guide lists hukou cancellation and foreign settlement evidence and assigns approval to the original-hukou SAFE office.
questions.missing: Naturalisation/permanent-residence dates, hukou cancellation certificate and property acquisition dates.
questions.why: These facts decide whether a one-off emigrant property transfer approval is possible.
questions.discover: Obtain certified immigration-status and hukou-cancellation documents and a dated property schedule; ask the original-hukou SAFE office whether it will accept an application.

questions.question: Is any part an inheritance from a person whose hukou was in mainland China?
questions.known: Inheritance transfer is a distinct route assigned to the deceased's hukou SAFE office; it requires inheritance, title and tax documents and must go to the heir's own overseas account.
questions.missing: Death certificate, relationship/inheritance proof, title documents, tax certificate and the deceased's hukou location.
questions.why: Using the ordinary income route for inherited capital would misstate the transaction.
questions.discover: Collect notarised or officially accepted inheritance and title documents; ask the deceased's hukou SAFE office for its current checklist.

questions.question: Which PRC bank holds the CNY, and exactly whose U.S. account will receive the USD?
questions.known: The property-transfer rule requires remittance to the applicant's own overseas account; Wise says from-CNY transfers can go only to another account the sender owns; SAFE rules distinguish own-account and cross-border transfers.
questions.missing: Bank name, branch, account title, your U.S. receiving bank and account ownership evidence.
questions.why: A third-party recipient, mismatched name or unsupported corridor can stop the transfer or trigger compliance review.
questions.discover: Get a bank letter with your exact account title and available services; open or confirm a U.S. account in the same name; ask the PRC bank to confirm the receiving-account details it will accept.

questions.question: What is the exact amount, currency and desired timing?
questions.known: This guide prices every US$10,000 step from the first to the last tier; published rate boards are dated and for reference only.
questions.missing: Your actual balance, whether interest accrues, and whether you need one payment or staged payments.
questions.why: Wire caps, annual quota/cash limits, FX movements and future tax years all depend on amount and timing.
questions.discover: Obtain an official balance letter; decide the target amount in USD; ask the bank whether a single or several remittances are possible and what rate applies on each date.

questions.question: Will the bank actually approve this source of funds and what exact rate/fees will it quote?
questions.known: Banks must reasonably review authenticity; BOC's published fee schedule allows separate agreements, promotions and local differences; its linked promotion page currently returns a 404; HSBC's tariff excludes other institutions' charges and taxes.
questions.missing: A written bank eligibility decision, executable rate, local fee schedule, correspondent/receiving fees and any monthly account fee.
questions.why: A published tariff is not approval, a quote, or an all-in cost.
questions.discover: Ask the branch for a written checklist, an executable rate and a full fee breakdown including intermediary and receiving charges; retain the reply. Do not rely on the web board alone.

questions.question: What prior U.S. foreign-account, asset and gift reports have been filed?
questions.known: FBAR is required when foreign-account aggregate value exceeds US$10,000 at any time; Form 8938 thresholds depend on residence and filing status; Form 3520 applies to large foreign gifts/bequests; Streamlined procedures require non-willful certification.
questions.missing: Prior-year returns, FinCEN filings, account maxima, gift documents and whether the IRS has contacted you.
questions.why: A low-tax transfer can become expensive if past reporting is missing; penalties are separate from conversion.
questions.discover: Obtain IRS account transcripts and prior returns; list each foreign account and its annual maximum; give the filing history to a U.S. tax professional before choosing a correction route.

questions.question: When and at what CNY/USD rate was the CNY acquired?
questions.known: The IRS says a spot rate is generally used when an item is received/paid/accrued, has no official exchange rate, and accepts a consistently used posted rate; a personal currency gain above US$$200 is not excluded by §988.
questions.missing: Acquisition dates, exchange rates, basis records and whether the later disposition is a personal transaction.
questions.why: Currency movement between acquisition and disposition can create U.S. ordinary gain or loss even though principal is not income.
questions.discover: Reconstruct each deposit's date and CNY/USD rate from bank and payroll records; choose a consistent posted rate with a tax professional; compute potential gain before transferring.

questions.question: Do FEIE, foreign tax credit or a treaty apply to the underlying income?
questions.known: The 2026 FEIE exclusion cap is $132,900 and the next-year cap is $137,300; the FTC is limited to qualifying tax on the same income and cannot be claimed on excluded income; treaty effects require the specific treaty text.
questions.missing: Tax home, abode, bona fide residence/physical presence, foreign tax paid, and treaty residence.
questions.why: Exclusion and credit rules interact; neither changes the principal, and a wrong election can create double work or penalties.
questions.discover: Give a U.S. tax professional your travel calendar, foreign tax receipts and income character; read the current treaty publication before claiming a treaty position.

questions.question: Is any part a gift or bequest from a foreign person?
questions.known: A U.S. person reports gifts/bequests from a nonresident alien or foreign estate above $100,000 and from foreign entities above $20,573 in 2026; related-party gifts are aggregated.
questions.missing: Donor identity, donor status, relationship, gift documents and aggregation across related parties.
questions.why: A mistaken gift label affects both Form 3520 reporting and PRC source-of-funds review.
questions.discover: Collect signed gift statements and donor-status evidence; aggregate all related-party gifts for the tax year; ask a U.S. tax professional to review Form 3520.

questions.question: Will any cash or monetary instruments be physically carried?
questions.known: PRC rules allow up to US$5,000 without a carry permit, require a bank permit above that up to US$10,000, and generally prohibit more except special SAFE permits; U.S. rules require reporting more than US$10,000 at one time.
questions.missing: Travel plan, denominations, permits, security arrangements and group totals.
questions.why: Physical carrying adds permit, reporting, security and deposit/conversion unknowns; families/groups are aggregated for CBP.
questions.discover: Ask the bank and SAFE what permit is required; obtain the permit; keep purchase and withdrawal memos; file the U.S. report when the collective amount exceeds the threshold.

questions.question: Has the bank/SAFE confirmed a direct cross-border RMB route in writing?
questions.known: PBOC supports banks handling current-account cross-border RMB settlement for individuals, including lawful salary, under bank due-diligence and AML duties, but publishes no personal fee, rate or general capital/savings route here.
questions.missing: Written legal basis, permitted purpose, tariff, limit, exchange rate and receiving-bank terms.
questions.why: A generic policy supporting current-account settlement does not establish a lawful route for moving an accumulated capital balance.
questions.discover: Ask the bank for the exact rule, permitted transaction category, written approval and full price; if it cannot provide them, leave the route unused and blank.
